Apple's first foldable iPhone is expected to make its official debut in just over a week. Sources indicate that during the development phase, Apple internally considered launching a brand-new Apple Pencil designed specifically for the iPhone Ultra, but this stylus is almost certainly one that will never actually hit the market.

The information comes from Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, who specifically emphasised that this Apple Pencil will not make an appearance at next month's launch event. Nevertheless, he still described in detail the stylus's intended design and anticipated operation.

The stylus was originally designed differently from the Apple Pencil currently used with the iPad lineup; it was designed to be shorter, to match the shorter body proportions of the iPhone Ultra. However, similar to the iPad version of the Apple Pencil, it was originally designed to attach magnetically to the side of the device for convenient storage and charging.

He noted that holding this stylus while using the iPhone Ultra would be rather awkward, because the stylus would attach to the side of the device; by contrast, when using an iPad in landscape mode, the stylus attaches to the top.

He also mentioned that this stylus is highly likely to leave "unsightly marks" on the more fragile inner screen of the iPhone Ultra.

He ultimately speculated that the main reason Apple decided not to release this stylus was a reluctance to go against the stance Steve Jobs insisted upon when introducing the original iPhone — "Who wants a stylus?"

Personally, I still think an Apple Pencil designed specifically for the iPhone Ultra would be quite practical, but it looks like we won't be seeing this stylus anytime soon.

After the latest round of price hikes, you may want to keep an eye on Apple's refurbished product store — you just might find a great bargain, as various refurbished products can save you quite a bit of money, including iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Apple TV.
